prompts.prompt: Write a cold outreach email to a potential mentor in my field — we've never spoken.
prompts.expected: Fires this skill. Produces two or three variants differing in directness/warmth, each labeled with its angle and when to use it, not one email restated three ways.

prompts.prompt: I need to email a client to push back on scope creep without burning the relationship.
prompts.expected: Fires this skill. Recognizes the strategic tension (assertive vs. relationship-preserving) and offers variants that trade off directness against warmth.

prompts.prompt: Can you give me a couple of options for a follow-up email? They haven't responded to my message from two weeks ago.
prompts.expected: Fires this skill — explicit request for options on a follow-up, a classic strategic-angle situation (gentle nudge vs. direct check-in vs. offering an easy out).

prompts.prompt: Email my team that the server will be down for an hour tonight for maintenance.
prompts.expected: Does not fire this skill. Routine, single-purpose, informational email with no real strategic angle — belongs to writing-assistant, which produces one clean draft.

prompts.prompt: Rewrite this email to sound more formal: 'hey just checking if you got my last message'.
prompts.expected: Does not fire this skill. This is editing existing text for tone, not choosing between outreach strategies — writing-assistant's job.

prompts.prompt: Summarize this email thread into three bullet points.
prompts.expected: Does not fire this skill. Condensing existing content is source-summarizer's job, not drafting.
